Rustic Country Bread

Served at: Feast of the Ass

Makes 1 large loaf (Serves 8-10)Prep 3 hours 30 minutes (includes rising time)Cook 40-45 minutes

This hearty, rustic country bread, or 'pain de campagne,' would have been a staple at any medieval celebration, including the Feast of the Ass. Its robust crust and soft, chewy interior make it perfect for soaking up stews or serving alongside cheeses, embodying the simple, nourishing spirit of historical feasts.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) warm water (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast (one standard packet)
  • 1 teaspoon (4 g) granulated sugar or honey (optional, for yeast activation)
  • 2 cups (240 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1 1/2 cups (180 g) whole wheat flour
  • 2 teaspoons (10 g) fine sea salt
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil, plus more for greasing

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and sugar (if using). Stir gently and let sit for 5-10 minutes, until foamy.
  2. Add the all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, and salt to the yeast mixture. Stir with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms and all the flour is incorporated.
  3. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more all-purpose flour, one tablespoon at a time.
  4. Lightly grease a clean large bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel.
  5. Let the dough rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.
  6. Gently punch down the dough to release the air. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and shape it into a round or oval loaf.
  7. Place the shaped loaf onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, or into a floured banneton or proofing basket. If using a baking sheet, you can score the top of the loaf with a sharp knife or razor blade (a few shallow cuts).
  8. Cover the loaf loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise for another 45-60 minutes, or until it has nearly doubled in size again.
  9. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C) with a baking stone or heavy baking sheet inside, if you have one, for at least 30 minutes before baking. If you have a Dutch oven, preheat it with the lid on.
  10. If using a baking sheet, carefully transfer the parchment paper with the loaf onto the preheated stone/sheet. If using a Dutch oven, carefully transfer the loaf into the hot Dutch oven.
  11. Bake for 20 minutes. If using a Dutch oven, remove the lid after 20 minutes.
  12. Reduce the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and continue baking for another 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is deeply golden brown and the internal temperature of the bread reaches 200-210°F (93-99°C).
  13. Remove the bread from the oven and transfer it to a wire rack to cool completely before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For an extra crispy crust, place a shallow pan of hot water on the bottom rack of your oven during the first 15 minutes of baking to create steam.
  • Don't rush the cooling process; slicing hot bread can make it gummy. Allow it to cool completely for the best texture and flavor.
  • Experiment with adding a tablespoon of seeds (like sunflower or flax) to the dough for added texture and nutrition, a common practice in rustic breads.
